title: CD70/CLL-1.BiCAR T Cells for Relapsed or Refractory AML
official: Chimeric Antigen Receptor Treatment Targeting AML Through CD70 (SEventy) Boosted CLL-1.CAR
summary:
This study is for patients who have a type of blood cancer called acute myeloid leukemia (AML) that has come back or has not gone away after standard treatments. The study will test a new kind of treatment made from a patient's own white blood cells, called BiCAR T cells.

T cells are special infection-fighting cells in the immune system. In this study, the patient's T cells are collected from their blood and changed in the laboratory to recognize and attack AML cells. The modified cells, called BiCAR T cells, have been given two "receptors" that help them find and destroy cancer cells in two ways - one that recognizes a target called CLL-1, and another that recognizes CD70, a protein found on many leukemia cells.

This "two-target" approach is designed to help the T cells find more cancer cells and stay active longer in the body. After the T cells are changed in the lab, they are given back to the patient through an IV.

Before receiving the BiCAR T cells, patients will get a short course of lymphodepleting chemotherapy. This step, called lymphodepletion, helps make space in the body for the new T cells to grow and work more effectively.

The main goals of this study are to:

1. Find the safest and most effective dose of BiCAR T cells;
2. Learn about possible side effects; and
3. See how the treatment affects leukemia cells in the blood and bone marrow.
conditions: Relapsed or Refractory Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML)

interventions.name: Autologous BiCAR T cells targeting CLL-1 and CD70

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

PROCUREMENT INCLUSION CRITERIA:

* 1\. Diagnosis of primary refractory or relapsed Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) with the exception of acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL). Patients with targetable mutations should have failed or be ineligible for targeted therapies (e.g. FLT3 inhibitors, IDH inhibitors or anti-CD33 drug conjugate)

  * Primary refractory or resistant disease, defined for purposes of procurement as not achieving complete remission (CR) (i.e., a remaining blast count of 5% or more) after 1 to 2 cycles of intense induction therapy.
  * Relapse is defined as (1) hematologic relapse after complete remission based on bone marrow blasts greater than or equal to 5%, or reappearance of blasts in the blood, or development of extramedullary disease; (2) molecular relapse after minimal residual disease (MRD) negative, complete remission based on reoccurrence of MRD as assessed by RT-qPCR or by multi-parametric flow cytometry (MFC)
* 2\. CLL-1 positive leukemia with at least 26% CLL-1+ blasts by flow cytometry or immunohistochemistry (staining can be pending at time of procurement)
* 3\. Age ≤ 75 years. NOTE: The first three (3) patients treated on the study will be ≥16 years of age.
* 4\. Hemoglobin ≥ 7.0 g/dL (can be transfused)
* 5\. If apheresis required to collect blood:

  * PT and APTT \< 1.5x ULN
  * Serum Creatinine\< 2 x ULN
  * AST \< 5 x ULN.
* 6\. Informed Consent obtained.

TREATMENT INCLUSION CRITERIA:

* 1\. Diagnosis of primary refractory or relapsed Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) with the exception of acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL). Patients with targetable mutations should have failed or be ineligible for targeted therapies (e.g. FLT3 inhibitors, IDH inhibitors or anti-CD33 drug conjugate).

  * Primary refractory or resistant disease as defined by not achieving complete remission (CR) (i.e., a remaining blast count of 5% or more) after 1-2 cycles of intense induction therapy. Patients with no reduction in blast count after the first cycle or with p53 mutations without CR after the first cycle of intense induction therapy are also considered primary refractory.
  * Relapse is defined as (1) hematologic relapse after complete remission based on bone marrow blasts greater than or equal to 5%, or reappearance of blasts in the blood, or development of extramedullary disease; (2) molecular relapse after minimal residual disease (MRD) negative, complete remission based on reoccurrence of MRD as assessed by RT-qPCR or by multi-parametric flow cytometry (MFC)
* 2\. Confirmation from the patient's primary physician team of a suitable allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) donor OR Documentation from the patient's primary physician team that patient declines a potential subsequent HSCT
* 3\. CLL-1 positive leukemia with at least 26% CLL-1+ cells by flow cytometry or immunohistochemistry (tissue)
* 4\. No systemic chemotherapy at least 1 week prior to treatment on study and must be recovered from all acute toxic effects of prior chemotherapy at time of treatment
* 5\. Age ≤ 75 years. NOTE: The first three (3) patients treated on the study will be ≥16 years of age. Safety data review and FDA approval required before enrolling pediatric patients thereafter
* 6\. Hemoglobin ≥ 7.0 g/dL (can be transfused)
* 7\. Total bilirubin \< 3 times the upper limit of normal
* 8\. AST/ALT \< 5 times the upper limit of normal
* 9\. Estimated GFR ≥ 50ml/min
* 10\. Pulse oximetry of \> 90% on room air
* 11\. Karnofsky or Lansky score of ≥ 60%
* 12\. Sexually active patients must be willing to utilize one of the more effective birth control methods during the study and for 6 months after study is concluded.
* 13\. Informed Consent Obtained

Exclusion Criteria:

PROCUREMENT EXCLUSION CRITERIA

* 1\. Diagnosis of acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL)
* 2\. Active infection (bacterial, fungal or viral) requiring ongoing treatment without improvement.
* 3\. Uncontrolled active infection with HIV or HTLV
* 4\. Active second cancer or cancer treated ≤ 2 years prior to enrollment (except non-melanoma skin cancer or in situ breast or cervical cancer)
* 5\. Ongoing treatment with immune suppression for prophylaxis/treatment of GVHD including high dose steroids (e.g., prednisone or equivalent greater than 0.5 mg/kg/day)

TREATMENT EXCLUSION CRITERIA

* 1\. Diagnosis of acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL)
* 2\. Currently receiving any investigational agents. (Applies to investigational cancer directed agents administered within 4 weeks or 5 half-lives whichever is shorter)
* 3\. Pregnant or lactating
* 4\. Uncontrolled infection with HIV, or HTLV. Patients with HIV are eligible if viral load is undetectable on therapy and CD4 count is \>350 mm3.
* 5\. Clinically significant bacterial, fungal, or viral infection requiring ongoing therapy without improvement
* 6\. Cardiac abnormalities:

  * Cardiac echocardiography with LVEF \<50%;
  * Cardiac dysfunction NYHA III or IV;
  * Clinically significant pericardial effusion. Confirmation of absence of these conditions must be obtained within 6 months of treatment.
* 7\. Presence of CNS disease: Defined as detectable cerebrospinal blast cells in a sample of CSF with ≥ 5 WBCs per mm3 or known CNS tumors/chloromas (repeat spinal tap or imaging within 4 weeks only required for leukemia patients with known CNS disease)
* 8\. Use of serotherapy with Campath or Anti-Thymocyte Globulin (ATG) within the last 28 days
* 9\. Use of Donor Lymphocyte Infusion (DLI) or other cellular therapy product within 28 days
* 10\. Acute GVHD ≥ Grade 2 or moderate to severe (formerly extensive) chronic GVHD
* 11\. Hyperleukocytosis (WBC ≥ 50K) or rapidly progressive disease that in the estimation of the investigator would compromise the ability of the patient to complete the initial 4 weeks of the study
